text: PYTHON ERROR TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE ModuleNotFoundError Description: ModuleNotFoundError occurs when Python cannot find the module that a program is trying to import. Common Cause: The required package may not be installed in the Python environment currently being used. Troubleshooting: Check whether the required package is installed in the active Python environment. For example, if a program imports the requests package, verify that requests is installed in the environment. Another possible cause is that the program is being executed with a different Python interpreter or virtual environment from the one where the package was installed. NameError Description: NameError occurs when Python encounters a name that has not been defined. Common Cause: A variable, function, or other name may be misspelled or may not have been defined before it is used. Troubleshooting: Check the spelling of the variable or function name. Verify that the name has been defined before the line where it is used. TypeError Description: TypeError occurs when an operation or function is applied to an object of an inappropriate type. Common Cause: The program may be trying to perform an operation using incompatible data types. Troubleshooting: Check the types of the values involved in the operation. Verify that function arguments have the expected types. IndexError Description: IndexError occurs when a sequence is accessed using an index that is outside the valid range. Common Cause: The program may be trying to access an element at an index that does not exist. Troubleshooting: Check the length of the list or sequence. Make sure the index is within the valid range. KeyError Description: KeyError occurs when a dictionary is accessed using a key that does not exist in the dictionary. Common Cause: The requested key may be missing from the dictionary. Troubleshooting: Check whether the key exists before accessing it. Verify that the key is spelled correctly.
